newsitem.title: INDONESIA: East Timor capital calm after Christmas killing.
newsitem.headline: East Timor capital calm after Christmas killing.

text.p: East Timor's capital Dili was calm on Wednesday as Catholic residents of the former Portuguese colony celebrated Christmas, a day after a soldier was beaten to death near the city's cathedral, police said.

"The situation today is safe and controlled, all Christians are celebrating Christmas in a good way. The city is calm and orderly and cars are moving in the streets as usual," East Timor police chief Colonel Yusuf Muharam told Reuters by telephone.
"It was only yesterday, there were disturbances between the crowd because of a misunderstanding," Muharam said.

He confirmed that one East Timorese soldier was beaten to death by a crowd of Catholic youths outside the city's main cathedral as thousands gathered to celebrate mass with 1996 Nobel peace laureate Bishop Carlos Belo.

Tens of thousands of people had flocked in from outside Dili to greet Belo, who returned on Tuesday from a European trip where he collected his award as well as met German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Pope John Paul.

Muharam said 11 people were still in hospital with wounds they received as a result of attacks by the crowd, mostly on soldiers or police in civilian clothes. Two of the injured were members of the public, he said.

Residents said the youths attacked the man outside the cathedral after he was found with a pistol and walkie-talkie radio, but Muharam said the soldier was joining the mass at which Belo called on Timorese to be united in peace.
They said rumours had been rife in recent days that an assassination attempt would be made on Belo, who last month said attempts on his life had been made in 1989 and 1991.
"Up to now we have not detained anybody, but we will," Muharam said.
Mostly Moslem Indonesia still maintains a large security force in East Timor more than 21 years after its December 1975 invasion.
Jakarta faces limited political and armed resistance to its rule in the territory, which it declared its 27th province in July 1976 in a move not yet recognised by the United Nations.
